record.notes: Introduced as Bill No. 29/2024, read the first time on 9 Sep 2024; Minister Josephine Teo moved the second reading on 15 Oct 2024, and the second and third readings took place that day. The Act commenced on 22 Jan 2025. It inserts s. 61MA into the Parliamentary Elections Act 1954 and s. 42LA into the Presidential Elections Act 1991, extends the Returning Officer's corrective directions to the new offence and lets candidates request them; a candidate who knowingly makes a false or misleading declaration in a request commits an illegal practice. The ban does not apply to private or domestic communications or to news published by authorised news agencies, and a person who did not know and had no reason to believe that the representation was false has a defence. In the second-reading speech the Minister also announced a Code of Practice under the Protection from Online Falsehoods and Manipulation Act requiring social media services to counter digitally generated or manipulated content at all times, to be issued in 2025.

verification.note: Recheck of 18 Oct 2026. Stored and read: Bill No. 29/2024 on parliament.gov.sg (copy of 11 Oct 2026, unchanged when checked on 18 Oct 2026), which gives the short title of the Act, the first reading, the offences, penalties and corrective directions; Minister Josephine Teo's second-reading speech of 15 Oct 2024 on MDDI's newsroom (secondary source, copy of 18 Oct 2026); and, stored in this run, the Elections Department's informal consolidation of the Parliamentary Elections Act 1954 (eld.gov.sg, version in force from 28 Mar 2025), whose legislative history lists Act 34 of 2024 with Bill 29/2024, first reading 9 Sep 2024, second and third readings 15 Oct 2024 and commencement 22 Jan 2025, and whose s. 61MA and related provisions carry the annotation '[Act 34 of 2024 wef 22/01/2025]'. The Act as published in the Acts Supplement on Singapore Statutes Online could not be stored (HTTP 403, also with the browser), so the date of assent is not recorded and the official_url remains the Bill as introduced. Version 1's identifier (the Bill number with the inserted sections in parentheses) is replaced by the Act number; the sections are in the notes. Version 1's account of first use at the 2025 General Election came from a law firm (Baker McKenzie), and its remark on the Online Safety (Relief and Accountability) Act 2025 rests on no stored file; both were removed from the notes.

notes.quote: Bill No. 29/2024. Read the first time on 9 September 2024.
First Reading : 9 September 2024 Second and Third Readings : 15 October 2024 Commencement : 22 January 2025
Madam Deputy Speaker, I beg to move, "That the Bill be now read a second time."

An Act to amend the Parliamentary Elections Act 1954 and the Presidential Elections Act 1991 to prohibit the publication of online election advertising containing certain digitally generated or manipulated content about candidates
A candidate commits an illegal practice if he or she —
any communication of content between 2 or more individuals that is of a private or domestic nature by electronic means;
any publication of any news relating to an election by an authorised news agency;
it is a defence for the person charged to prove, on a balance of probabilities, that the person did not know and had no reason to believe that the candidate did not in fact say or do the thing
will be required to prevent and counter the abuse of digitally generated or manipulated content at all times through an upcoming Code of Practice under POFMA
we intend to finalise the Code for issuance in 2025

judgment.status_reasoning: The ELD consolidation's legislative history gives commencement on 22 Jan 2025, and the consolidated Act (version in force from 28 Mar 2025) contains s. 61MA with the annotation '[Act 34 of 2024 wef 22/01/2025]'. 22 Jan 2025 is before today (18 Oct 2026), and nothing stored shows a repeal. 'In force' stands, now with date_in_force 2025-01-22. Binding as an Act of Parliament.
judgment.date_reasoning: date_published 2024-10-15 is the date of the second and third readings, i.e. passage by Parliament (ELD legislative history). The date of assent is in the Acts Supplement on Singapore Statutes Online, which could not be stored; passage is kept as the adoption date. date_in_force 2025-01-22 is the commencement date.
judgment.scope_reasoning: A law that is not AI-specific in form but whose operative content targets digitally generated or manipulated content, with generative AI given as the example; version 1 has it in scope with no scope_note and the precedents (operative instrument for deepfakes) would at most add a note. Left unchanged.
